newsitem.title: BRAZIL: CRT shr sale lifts Brazil telecom stocks, bolsa.
newsitem.headline: CRT shr sale lifts Brazil telecom stocks, bolsa.

text.p: The sale of a minority stake in Rio Grande do Sul state's telecom boosted Brazilian telecoms stock prices, sending Telesp soaring and prompting a rise Sao Paulo bourse, brokers said.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index was up one percent at 67,208 points, led by a 6.4 percent rise in preferred shares of Telesp to 207 reais, by 1600 local/1300 EST.

Brokers and analysts said the rise was spurred by today's sale of a 35-percent stake in Companhia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes (CRT) for 681 million reais ($655 million) to a Brazilian-Spanish group.
The CRT share sale was closely watched by the market, which viewed it as a litmus test for the upcoming privatization of Brazil's massive federal telecoms system, including giant Telebras.
The winning bid was 54.8 percent above the state-set base price of 440 million reais ($423 million).
Despite a protest by the group that presented the losing offer, the auction prompted the market to surge in the afternoon, brokers said.
"There was a complaint regarding the documentation, but whaever the outcome (of the protest), the auction was good and the market is rising," one dealer told Reuters.
While Telesp soared, other telecoms stocks posted moderate gains after the auction at 1330 local/1030 EST.
Bolsa benchmark, blue chip Telebras preferred, rose 1.25 percent to 77.20 reais while its voting common jumped 2.25 percent to 70.60 reais.
Meanwhile, Telebras' American Depositary Receipt (ADR) surged 2 1/4, or over three percent, to 74 1/2 on trhe New York Stock Exchange.
Locally, Telepar common rose 5.5 percent to 475 reais while its preferred climbed 2.3 percent to 482 reais.
Telerj rose 1.6 percent to 126 reais and its preferred climbed 1.24 percent to 119.50 reais.
Telemig moved up 3.4 percent to 117 reais while its preferred rose 0.4 percent to 113 reais.
